facts.fact_text: On 17 April 2011, the applicant participated in a demonstration organised by the opposition in Baku.
On 26 January 2013, the applicant participated in a demonstration organised by the opposition in Baku.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations of 17 April 2011 and 26 January 2013 were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations of 17 April 2011 and 26 January 2013 were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 17 April 2011.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 17 April 2011 at the place indicated by the organisers.
Shortly after the demonstration of 17 April 2011 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
Shortly after the demonstration of 26 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 17 April 2011 and taken to a police station.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 26 January 2013 and taken to a police station.
In the first case (17 April 2011), the first-instance court found that the applicant had participated or attempted to participate in an unauthorised demonstration.
In the second case (26 January 2013), the court found that the applicant had incited people to participate in an unlawful assembly.
In the second case (26 January 2013), the court found that the applicant had violated the rules on organising and holding assemblies.
By a decision of 18 April 2011, the first-instance court in the first case convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
By a decision of 18 April 2011, the first-instance court in the first case sentenced the applicant to five days' administrative detention.
By a decision of 26 January 2013, the court in the second case convicted the applicant under Article 298.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
By a decision of 26 January 2013, the court in the second case sentenced the applicant to a fine of 2,000 Azerbaijani manats (AZN).

At the time of both of the applicant's arrests (17 April 2011 and 26 January 2013), under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 17 April 2011, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that any breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen Azerbaijani manats (AZN).

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 17 April 2011, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with a lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five Azerbaijani manats (AZN) or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by administrative detention for a term of up to fifteen days.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 17 April 2011, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that an individual who is subject to administrative offence proceedings shall be given an opportunity to familiarise themselves with the administrative offence report.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 17 April 2011, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that an individual who is subject to administrative offence proceedings has the right to a copy of the administrative offence report.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences concerning breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced for the first time a punishment in the form of administrative detention of up to fifteen days for breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced community service as a new form of punishment for breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 increased the fine for breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies, fixing the amounts as follows: between AZN 300 and 600 for participants of an assembly; between AZN 1,500 and 3,000 for individuals who organise an assembly; between AZN 3,000 and 6,000 for persons in charge (vəzifəli şəxslər) who organise an assembly; and between AZN 15,000 and 30,000 for legal entities involved in the organisation of an assembly.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted that the place proposed by the organisers for the demonstration of 17 April 2011 was in an area with heavy traffic.

The administrative offence report issued on 17 April 2011 stated that by deliberately failing to comply with a lawful order from the police, the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

In the second case (arrest of 26 January 2013), the applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 298.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, which concerns breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies by an assembly organiser.
The police officers testified that the applicant had attempted to stage an unauthorised demonstration.
In the second case (26 January 2013), the police officers also testified that the applicant had incited others to participate in an unauthorised assembly.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 17 April 2011 at the place indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) proposed a different location for the demonstration of 17 April 2011, namely the yard of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail District, on the outskirts of Baku.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted that the place proposed by the organisers for the demonstration of 17 April 2011 was in an area with heavy traffic.

The organisers decided to hold the demonstrations in the centre of Baku, notwithstanding the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the demonstration of 17 April 2011 at the proposed location.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments increasing penalties for organisers of and participants in 'unauthorised' gatherings are likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression in Azerbaijan.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 stated that the sanctions which can now be imposed in Azerbaijan, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 stated that the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe is of the view that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 stated that the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe urges the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.

On an unspecified date, the applicant lodged a complaint before the General Prosecutor's Office asking it to conduct an investigation into ill-treatment allegedly committed by the police during her arrest on 17 April 2011.

By a letter of 25 May 2011, the General Prosecutor's Office informed the applicant's lawyer that the applicant's complaint of ill-treatment had been forwarded to the Baku City prosecutor's office for examination.
The letter of 25 May 2011 from the General Prosecutor's Office instructed the Baku City prosecutor's office to inform the applicant's lawyer about the results of the examination of the complaint.
On an unspecified date, the applicant was summoned to the Nasimi District prosecutor's office and questioned in connection with her complaint of ill-treatment.
According to the applicant, neither she nor her lawyer was informed about any actions taken by the authorities to investigate her complaint of ill-treatment.

According to the applicant, it was only after making enquiries about the outcome of the investigation, in January 2012, that the applicant managed to obtain a copy of an investigator's decision of 16 June 2011 refusing to open a criminal case.
The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 was produced by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 stated that the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe is deeply concerned by the recent amendments to the Law on Freedom of Assembly, the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which further erode the right to freedom of assembly.
